title: Scales and fingering
summary: Even scales with the standard fingerings, starting with the thumb crossing.

lessons.title: C major and the thumb crossing
lessons.summary: Eight notes with five fingers: where the thumb passes under.

blocks.text: A scale has eight notes but you have five fingers, so the hand has to shift. Going up in the right hand, the thumb passes under after finger 3. The fingering is 1 2 3, then 1 2 3 4 5.
C major, right hand, with fingering.
Keep the hand level as the thumb passes under. Move the thumb early, while finger 2 and 3 are playing, so it is already waiting over its key. Do not twist the wrist or lift the elbow to make room.
Coming down, finger 3 crosses over the thumb. The left hand mirrors this: going up it plays 5 4 3 2 1, then finger 3 crosses over, 3 2 1.

exercise.prompt: Play C major, right hand, up and down. Go slowly; the music waits for you.

blocks.text: After each scale the app shows how even your notes were in timing and in loudness. A common pattern is a bump at the crossing: the note after the thumb comes late or loud. If you see that, practise just the three notes around the crossing.

sources: Standard scale fingering as printed in common scale manuals; check against your own reference.

lessons.title: G, D and F major
lessons.summary: The same shape with one or two black keys, and one new fingering.

blocks.text: G major and D major use exactly the same fingering as C major. G major has one sharp, F♯. D major has two, F♯ and C♯.
F major has one flat, B♭. In the right hand the thumb cannot land on the black key, so the fingering changes: 1 2 3 4, then 1 2 3 4. The left hand keeps the usual fingering.

exercise.prompt: Play F major, right hand. The thumb passes under after finger 4.

sources: Standard scale fingering as printed in common scale manuals; check against your own reference.

lessons.title: A minor
lessons.summary: The minor scale that shares C major's notes, and its harmonic form.

blocks.text: A natural minor uses only white keys, like C major, but starts and ends on A. The fingering is the same as C major.

exercise.prompt: Play A natural minor, right hand.

blocks.text: Music in a minor key very often raises the seventh note by a half step, which pulls strongly back to the keynote. In A minor that note is G♯. This form is called the harmonic minor.

exercise.prompt: Play A harmonic minor, right hand. Listen for the wide step from F to G♯.

blocks.text: Greensleeves is in A minor and uses both G and G♯.
